title: Run problem
body:
I thought I ran this correctly:
`Installing the current project: allusgov (0.0)
`

But got a help-like return when running it:

```
allusgov % poetry run allusgov
The "poetry.dev-dependencies" section is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. Use "poetry.group.dev.dependencies" instead.
The currently activated Python version 3.9.13 is not supported by the project (>=3.10,<3.12).
Trying to find and use a compatible version. 
Using python3.10 (3.10.16)
Usage: allusgov [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Map the organization of the US Federal Government.

  This operates a three-stage pipeline: - Scrape the data from various
  directories (SOURCES) - Build a tree from the given SOURCES and export each
  source - Merge all data into a single tree, using fuzzy string matching

  Each stage is optional and will use cached data if available.

Options:
  --data-dir DIRECTORY  Directory to store data and cache files
  -v, --verbosity LVL   Either CRITICAL, ERROR, WARNING, INFO or DEBUG
  --help                Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  all     Execute all steps in order: spider, export, and merge.
  spider  Scrape data from the specified sources.
  build   Build a tree for each of the given sources and optionally...

  dev     Development commands.
```

I thought maybe I'd need to add it here:
```
allusgov % ls data 
acronyms	cisagov		federalregister	opmgov		usagov		usgovmanual
budget		digitalregistry	merged		samgov		usaspending
% mkdir data2   
```

Best I can get is:

```
% poetry allgov all --data-dir data2
The requested command allgov does not exist.

Documentation: https://python-poetry.org/docs/cli/
```

What am I missing?

title: [Docs] Add missing docstrings to importer/ module
body:
### Overview

The importer/ code (files inside allusgov/importer/) is missing helpful docstrings. Docstrings are short explanations you put at the top of a function, class, or module so others (and your future self!) know what it does, what inputs it expects, and what it returns.

This task is about adding clear, beginner-friendly docstrings to every function and class in that folder.

### Background

Right now, if someone new looks at the importer code, they have to read through all the logic to figure out what’s happening. That can be hard if you don’t know the project yet.

Adding docstrings will:
	•	Help new contributors understand the code faster.
	•	Make our codebase easier to use and maintain.
	•	Keep our style consistent with tools like pydocstyle (which we already run in CI).

### References

Here are resources that explain how to write good Python docstrings:
	•	[PEP 257 – Docstring Conventions](https://peps.python.org/pep-0257/)
	•	[Google Python Style Guide (docstrings section)](https://google.github.io/styleguide/pyguide.html#38-comments-and-docstrings)
	•	[pydocstyle documentation](http://www.pydocstyle.org/en/stable/)

Tip: We recommend Google-style docstrings (with Args:, Returns:, Raises: sections) because they’re easy to read.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every function and class in allusgov/importer/ has a docstring.
- [ ] Each docstring explains in plain language what the code does.
- [ ] Parameters, return values, and possible errors are included where it makes sense.
- [ ] uv run pydocstyle allusgov/importer passes with no errors.

title: [Refactor] Add type hints to normalize_name.py
body:
### Overview

The file allusgov/processor/normalize_name.py doesn’t use Python’s type hints, which help readers (and tools like mypy) know what types each function expects and returns. Adding type hints is a great beginner-friendly way to get comfortable with static typing in Python.

### Background

Type hints (e.g. def foo(x: str) -> int:) make code clearer and enable tools to catch mistakes before runtime. We already run mypy in CI, so this will help us maintain higher quality.

### References

•	[PEP 484 – Type Hints](https://peps.python.org/pep-0484/)
	•	[mypy — Optional Static Typing for Python](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/)
	•	[Real Python: Beginner’s Guide to Python Type Checking](https://realpython.com/python-type-checking/)



### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All functions and methods in normalize_name.py have complete type annotations (parameters and return types).
- [ ] CI (uv run mypy allusgov/processor) runs with zero type errors for that file.
- [ ] Any imported third-party types (e.g., TreebankWordTokenizer) are properly imported or referenced via typing.

title: [Testing] Write a unit test for DigitalRegistryImporter
body:
### Overview

The class DigitalRegistryImporter in allusgov/importer/digitalregistry_importer.py has no direct tests. Writing a simple pytest for its clean_dict method (and a basic build() scenario) will teach how to test classes and edge cases.

### Background

Unit tests give confidence that code changes don’t break functionality. For practice, focus on:
	1.	Passing it a small sample JSON-like dict with nested empty values.
	2.	Verifying that clean_dict removes None and empty dicts.

### References

•	[pytest Documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/)
	•	[Writing Your First Tests — pytest](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/getting-started.html)
	•	[Mocking with pytest](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/how-to/monkeypatch.html)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Create tests/test_digitalregistry_importer.py.
- [ ] Write at least two tests for clean_dict(): one simple flat dict, one nested dict scenario.
- [ ] (Bonus) Test that build() runs without errors for a minimal self.data sample.

title: [DevEx] Improve CLI help text with examples
body:
### Overview

When you run uv run allusgov --help (and subcommands like uv run allusgov merge --help), the descriptions are minimal. Adding a few real-world examples under each command will help beginners know how to use the tool.

### Background

Good CLI help text guides users on:
	•	Required vs optional flags
	•	Example commands (e.g. “Scrape SAM.gov and export JSON tree”)

### References

•	[Python Click: Adding Examples to Help](https://click.palletsprojects.com/en/8.1.x/#help-and-documentation)
	•	[Scrapy Cli Reference](https://docs.scrapy.org/en/latest/topics/commands.html)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Update cli.py (or wherever help text is defined) to include 2–3 example usages for the top-level command.
- [ ] Update subcommand help (e.g. spider, merge) with at least 1 example each.
- [ ] Run uv run allusgov --help and confirm examples appear and formatting looks clean.

title: [Data] Add seed acronym JSON files in data/acronyms/
body:
### Overview

The code expects data/acronyms/acronyms.json and data/acronyms/data.json to exist for normalization, but those files are missing or empty. We need to provide a starter JSON with a few common federal acronyms (e.g., "NASA": "National Aeronautics and Space Administration").

### Background

NormalizeName’s acronym list comes from those JSON files. Without seed data, normalization may miss common acronyms. Providing a small seed helps demonstrate the format for future contributors.

### References

•	[JSON File Format](https://www.json.org/json-en.html)
	•	[Example Acronym List](https://ucsd.libguides.com/govspeak/acronyms)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Create data/acronyms/acronyms.json with at least 5 entries, for example:
```json
{
  "NASA": "National Aeronautics and Space Administration",
  "EPA": "Environmental Protection Agency",
  "FBI": "Federal Bureau of Investigation",
  "DHS": "Department of Homeland Security",
  "USAID": "United States Agency for International Development"
}
```
- [ ] Create data/acronyms/data.json as needed by the code (can mirror acronyms.json).
- [ ] Update README or CONTRIBUTING to explain how to add more acronyms.

title: [Refactor] Standardize logging across all spiders
body:
### Overview

Right now each spider in allusgov/spider/ uses the logger differently (some use logger.info, others print). We need a consistent pattern so that every spider logs via our shared cli_options.logger and follows the same format.

### Background

Consistent logging helps when you run multiple spiders in one crawl. It also makes troubleshooting easier. We already configure a root logger—just ensure every spider does something like:
```python
from .cli_options import logger
logger.info("Starting spider %s", spider_name)
```

### References

•	[Python Logging HOWTO](https://docs.python.org/3/howto/logging.html)
	•	[Structuring Logs with formatters](https://docs.python.org/3/howto/logging.html#logging-basic-tutorial)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every file in allusgov/spider/ uses logger from cli_options, not print.
- [ ] Log messages follow the pattern: logger.<level>(f"<module>: message", args…).
- [ ] Update one example spider docstring to show the logging pattern.
- [ ] CI warnings/errors for unused imports or prints are resolved (run uv run pylint allusgov/spider).

title: [Data] Add JSON Schema validation for merged outputs
body:
### Overview

After merging, we export JSON files in data/merged/. We should define a JSON Schema that describes the expected structure (e.g., each node has name, children, optional normalized_name) and validate each output against it.

### Background

Schema validation catches unexpected changes early. Contributors can run a script validate_merged.py to check outputs locally.

### References

•	[JSON Schema Introduction](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/)
	•	[python-jsonschema Library](https://python-jsonschema.readthedocs.io/)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Create schemas/merged.schema.json describing the merged tree format.
- [ ] Add a script scripts/validate_merged.py that loads each file in data/merged/ and validates against the schema.
- [ ] Integrate this script into CI (e.g., add uv run python scripts/validate_merged.py to tests.yml).
- [ ] All existing merged outputs pass validation.

title: [DevEx] Implement diff tool for comparing two merged datasets
body:
### Overview

We want a small CLI command allusgov diff <file1> <file2> that shows how two merged JSON trees differ (added/removed nodes). This helps track changes between budget years.

### Background

A simple dict or tree‐walk diff can list node paths that exist in one file but not the other. This is a standalone script, no UI needed.

### References

•	[DeepDiff Python Library](https://zepworks.com/deepdiff/current/)
	•	[Scrapy Command Extensions](https://docs.scrapy.org/en/latest/topics/commands.html)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add new subcommand diff under cli.py.
- [ ] Use DeepDiff or custom logic to compare two JSON files.
- [ ] Print a concise list of node paths added/removed.
- [ ] Add tests for a small example pair of JSON trees.

title: [Feature] Add Parquet exporter for analytics workflows
body:
### Overview

Right now we export CSV and JSON. For big-data workflows, Parquet is more efficient. Add an exporter class ParquetExporter that writes data/merged/merged.parquet.

### Background

Parquet files are columnar and compress well. We can use pandas or pyarrow to write a DataFrame version of the flat JSON.

### References

•	[pandas to_parquet](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.to_parquet.html)
	•	[Apache Arrow Python Tutorial](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/python/)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Create allusgov/exporter/parquet_exporter.py with class ParquetExporter.
- [ ] Register it in settings.EXPORTERS so uv run allusgov --export parquet works.
- [ ] Write merged flat JSON into a Parquet file.
- [ ] Add a test that reads the Parquet back and checks key columns.

title: [Refactor] Expand NormalizeName rules for acronyms and spacing
body:
### Overview

NormalizeName currently handles basic whitespace and capitalization. Real agency names often have tricky acronyms (e.g., U.S. EPA-Office → U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Office). Enhance fix_split_word_acronyms and related logic to catch these.

### Background

Better acronym handling reduces manual corrections later. We can start by adding new unit tests that fail, then updating the algorithm.

### References

•	[Normalizer Patterns in NLP](https://nlp.stanford.edu/)
	•	[Regular Expression HOWTO](https://docs.python.org/3/howto/regex.html)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Identify and write tests for at least 3 tricky name cases.
- [ ] Update normalize_name.py to handle those cases.
- [ ] All new tests pass.
- [ ] CI coverage does not decrease.

title: [Feature] Make importer settings configurable via YAML
body:
### Overview

Currently settings.SOURCES and API endpoints are hard-coded in settings.py. Allow users to override or add sources via a config.yml file (listing name, importer_class, api_url, etc.).

### Background

Config-driven design empowers users to add new data sources without touching code.

### References

•	[PyYAML Usage](https://pyyaml.org/wiki/PyYAMLDocumentation)
	•	[Dynamic Imports in Python](https://docs.python.org/3/library/importlib.html)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Create config.yml schema for sources (in project root).
- [ ] Modify settings.py to load from config.yml if it exists, fallback to defaults.
- [ ] Document the new config file format in README.
- [ ] Add tests that simulate a custom config with a dummy importer.

title: [Data] Add per-source fuzzy match thresholds in merger
body:
### Overview

Right now the merger uses one global threshold for all sources. Allow each source to specify its own threshold in settings.py or via config, so we can fine-tune matching accuracy.

### Background

Some sources have more consistent names—requires high threshold. Others are noisy and need a lower threshold.

### References

•	[FuzzyWuzzy Library](https://github.com/seatgeek/fuzzywuzzy)
	•	[Configuration Patterns](https://12factor.net/)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Extend settings.SOURCES to include optional merge_threshold per source.
- [ ] Modify Merger to read that threshold when merging each tree.
- [ ] Write tests covering at least two threshold scenarios.
- [ ] Document behavior in README.

title: [Feature] Enable incremental spider runs with caching
body:
### Overview

Rather than re-download all pages, add a --since DATE flag to spiders so they only fetch new or updated records. Store a local cache of last‐run timestamps.

### Background

This saves time and avoids hammering APIs. We can store last‐modified headers or page IDs to skip already‐seen items.

### References

•	[Scrapy HTTP Caching](https://docs.scrapy.org/en/latest/topics/downloader-middleware.html#httpcache-middleware-settings)
	•	[Working with Dates in Python](https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add --since YYYY-MM-DD option to spider subcommand.
- [ ] Implement caching logic (e.g., using scrapy.extensions.httpcache).
- [ ] Document flag usage in README and help text.
- [ ] Test that a second run with --since only fetches delta.

title: [Data] Track provenance metadata in merged datasets
body:
### Overview

When merging nodes, include an attribute sources: [“samgov”, “opmgov”] on each node to show which original sources contributed to it.

### Background

Knowing provenance helps data consumers trust which sources back each node and can filter by source later.

### References

•	[Provenance Data Models (W3C)](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-overview/)
	•	[Adding Attributes to bigtree Nodes](https://pypi.org/project/bigtree/)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Update merger logic to collect source_name for each merged node.
- [ ] Include sources list in final node attributes.
- [ ] Export sources in JSON, CSV, and other formats.
- [ ] Add unit tests verifying provenance for a merged example.

title: [Export] Enhance DOT exporter to include node attributes
body:
### Overview

The current DOT exporter only outputs node names, losing valuable attributes (like normalized_name). Modify it to emit node-level attributes as DOT labels or properties.

### Background

Graph viewers (e.g., Graphviz) can display labels if provided. Including attributes improves visualization.

### References

•	[Graphviz DOT Language Guide](https://graphviz.org/doc/info/lang.html)
	•	[bigtree exporter.py example](https://github.com/CivicActions/allusgov/issues/allusgov/exporter/exporter.py)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Modify DOT exporter to include at least two attributes per node (e.g., normalized_name, source).
- [ ] Ensure the resulting .dot file still parses without errors.
- [ ] Add a test that loads the .dot into a pygraphviz or similar and checks for attribute presence.

title: [Docs] Expand CONTRIBUTING.md with step-by-step dev setup
body:
### Overview

Our CONTRIBUTING.md outlines high-level guidelines but doesn’t show how to set up the project locally from scratch. New contributors need a clear, step-by-step guide: clone, install dependencies, run tests, and build.

### Background

A good contributing guide reduces onboarding friction. It should include commands like uv sync, uv run pytest, and pointers to configure config.yml.

### References

•	[Example CONTRIBUTING.md (GitHub)](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
	•	[GitHub Docs: Setting Up a Project for Contribution](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-contributing-to-projects)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add a “Getting Started” section in CONTRIBUTING.md with:
	1.	Clone the repo
	2.	Install Python 3.12+
	3.	Install uv and dependencies (uv sync)
	4.	Running tests (uv run pytest)
	5.	Running CLI (uv run allusgov --help)
- [ ] Include troubleshooting tips (e.g., fixing missing dependencies).
- [ ] Link back to README where appropriate.

title: [Docs] Add real CLI usage examples to README
body:
### Overview

The README’s “Usage” section shows uv run allusgov but no real-world examples. We should add 3–4 practical commands, e.g.:
```markdown
# Scrape all sources and export JSON:
uv run allusgov all-steps --sources samgov,cisagov --export json

# Merge just SAM.gov and USA.gov:
uv run allusgov merge --merge-base samgov --sources samgov,usagov
```

### Background

Concrete examples help users understand flags and workflows. They also serve as living documentation for common tasks.

### References

•	[Example CONTRIBUTING.md (GitHub)](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
	•	[GitHub Docs: Setting Up a Project for Contribution](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-contributing-to-projects)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Under “Usage” in README.md, add at least 4 example commands covering:
	- [ ] Full pipeline (all-steps)
	- [ ] Spider only
	- [ ] Merge only
	- [ ] Export only
- [ ] Use fenced code blocks for clarity.
- [ ] Ensure examples run without errors (update any flags if outdated).

title: [Docs] Create tutorial notebook: scrape → merge → export
body:
### Overview

A Jupyter notebook demonstrating end-to-end usage will help Python learners. 

It should:
1.	Run spiders for one source (e.g., samgov)
2.	Build and inspect the tree in Python
3.	Merge two trees and visualize output
4.	Export to JSON/CSV and load into pandas

### Background

Notebooks are interactive and lower the barrier to entry. They let learners tweak parameters and see results immediately.

### References

•	[Jupyter Notebook Basics](https://jupyter.org/)
	•	[README-driven Notebooks Example](https://github.com/mwaskom/seaborn/blob/master/examples/many_pairwise_correlations.ipynb)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add notebooks/tutorial.ipynb covering the four steps above.
- [ ] Include explanatory markdown cells before each code block.
- [ ] Ensure all cells run top-to-bottom without errors.
- [ ] Commit outputs or include instructions to download data before running.

title: [DevEx] Improve CI pipeline with coverage reporting in PRs
body:
### Overview

Our CI runs tests and generates coverage.xml, but it doesn’t publish a badge or post coverage summaries on PRs. Let’s integrate a coverage report (e.g., via Codecov or Coveralls) so contributors see coverage changes when they open a PR.

### Background

Visible coverage metrics encourage adding tests and help maintain quality. A badge in the README is also motivating.

### References

•	[Codecov GitHub Action](https://github.com/codecov/codecov-action)
	•	[GitHub Actions: Uploading coverage reports](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/automating-builds-and-tests/building-and-testing-python#upload-code-coverage-results)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add a step in .github/workflows/tests.yml to upload coverage.xml to Codecov (or similar).
- [ ] Add a coverage badge to README.md.
- [ ] Verify that a sample PR shows coverage summary in the checks.

title: [Docs] Document new data source workflow using template
body:
### Overview

Contributors can propose new sources via .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/new_data_source.yml. We need a guide in README.md or CONTRIBUTING.md explaining how to use that template, what fields to fill, and how we process submissions.

### Background

Even with a template, contributors need context: where to find sample code, how to write a new spider, and how to run tests for that source.

title: feat: adding importlib to load config dynamically.
body:
# 📝 Summary

Moving sources and exporters to `config.yaml` and dynamically loading them.

> **Issue:** #22 
---

## 📖 Description

This PR allows users to add sources (spiders and importers) and exporters to a YAML file (`config.yaml`), and import modules by name at runtime and loads those modules into the `settings.py` dictionary. Previously hard-coded values didn't use the complete dotted name to the package for instance `importer.importer.Importer` was simply `importer.Importer` since the modules were imported into the `settings.py` file. `importlib` needed a more complete path to work properly so the `config.yaml` file contains the complete dotted name.

This PR also include `.idea/` files used by the JetBrains IDE PyCharm. They are added following the guidelines specified by [JetBrains](https://intellij-support.jetbrains.com/hc/en-us/articles/206544839-How-to-manage-projects-under-Version-Control-Systems) and using the [JetBrains .gitignore](https://github.com/github/gitignore/blob/main/Global/JetBrains.gitignore)

title: feat: track provenance across merged government data
body:
Fixes #25.

## Summary

Implements CivicActions/allusgov#25.

- records a deterministic `sources` list on nodes that actually originate from each input source
- unions provenance when fuzzy matching merges two records
- preserves provenance on unmatched child nodes moved into the merged tree
- keeps `full_name()` fallback working when provenance metadata is present
- renders merged text output from the explicit provenance list instead of treating metadata keys as sources
- adds a sequential three-source regression, including a node that exists only in the second and third sources
- asserts that merged provenance survives text, flat JSON, and CSV export

Existing JSON/CSV/graph exporters already consume node attributes, so the new metadata flows through their normal all-attribute paths.

## Verification

Static/diff review completed. The regression tests are committed but **not executed** in this environment (Python 3.12 / project dependencies unavailable). On head `5f9dac8`, upstream Actions conclude `action_required`, not pass. Keeping this draft until native tests and lint pass.

## Repository note

`CONTRIBUTING.md` says to branch from `develop`, but the current upstream repository exposes no `develop` branch. This branch is therefore based on the current `main` head.
